problem: writeExportFile swallows every mkdir/writeFile failure (it only logs, and only when KERYX_VERBOSE is set). Its caller runHistoryExport (line 122) then proceeds and prints `exported N run(s) to <file>` (line 131) with exit code 0, so a failed write is reported as success. Violates error-handling.mdc Rule 3 / Iron Law 1. Class scope: the only write-path catch in the diff; the other catch (line 128-130) is a commented display-only fallback and is fine.
impact: A user or script exporting to an unwritable path (read-only dir, EACCES, ENOSPC) is told the export succeeded and attaches a missing or stale file to a review or flow journal; nothing surfaces the failure unless verbose mode is on.

problem: Stale doc comment: collectRunRows claims it 'Returns the runs oldest first', but it only filters listWikiRuns, which is documented and implemented as newest first (src/wiki/history.ts:495-508 sorts descending). No reversal exists anywhere in the export path.
impact: The next reader trusts the comment about row order in the exported file; the comment asserts a behaviour that has no code path.

Returns the runs

problem: The command-label normalisation chain (collapse newlines, collapse whitespace, trim, clip to MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH) is copied three times in this change: wiki-history-export.ts:49-53, wiki-history-export.ts:56-60, and wiki-history.ts:47-51. MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH is shared but the logic that applies it is not.
impact: Whoever changes how labels are clipped or sanitised must edit three sites in two files and keep them in sync; the doc on MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH ('every rendered row') is only true while all three copies agree.

problem: renderRunLine takes a boolean flag `markdown` that selects between two different renderers (markdown row vs CSV row), and has four positional parameters of which `pages` is always `run.pages` at the only call site (line 119) and `at` is a derivation of `run.at`. The call reads `renderRunLine(run, at, run.pages, format === "md")`.
impact: Call sites must read the signature to decode the trailing boolean, and the redundant `pages` argument invites passing a value that disagrees with `run`. Two functions (renderCsvRow/renderMarkdownRow) taking the run would be clearer.

problem: The catch rethrows a new Error without `{ cause: error }` (the bound `error` is unused) and the message does not name the input (cwd / runs-log path). Violates error-handling.mdc Rule 5 / Iron Law 3 and Rule 2.
impact: Whoever debugs a failed export loses the original error (parse failure vs EACCES vs missing dir) and does not learn which runs log was read.

problem: runHistoryExport is ~57 lines (75-132) and does several separable jobs at different levels: argv parsing and validation of --export/--format/--since (including inline regex date normalisation at line 100), filtering orchestration, timestamp reformatting per row (line 118), file writing, and realpath-based display formatting.
impact: The option parsing cannot be unit-tested or reused apart from the file write; extracting a parseExportOptions(args) returning a typed options object would leave a short orchestration function.

problem: Three usage texts in the same change document the same command differently: HISTORY_USAGE omits --since and --command, while EXPORT_USAGE (wiki-history-export.ts:13) and the wiki help (wiki.ts:924) list them.
impact: A user reading the `wiki history` usage error does not learn the filter flags exist; the next editor has three strings to keep aligned.
